metric.why: A facility can have enough total cooling and still starve individual racks; airflow and pressure sensors find recirculation, bypass, and leaks that temperature averages hide.
metric.definition: Cubic feet per minute delivered through the room or containment system, and the pressure differential that drives it through equipment rather than around it.

reading.body:
Airflow and static pressure track the cubic feet per minute delivered through a room or containment system and the pressure differential driving that air through equipment rather than around it.

A facility can have enough total cooling capacity and still starve individual racks, because airflow and pressure sensors catch recirculation, bypass, and leaks that temperature averages alone do not reveal. That distinction matters because a facility-wide temperature reading can look normal even while specific racks are effectively being cooled by air that never reached them, which is exactly the failure mode this metric is built to catch.

It sits alongside temperature and humidity readings and liquid coolant temperature and flow rate under Cooling and climate, forming a set of measurements aimed at the same underlying question from different angles, whether cooling capacity that exists on paper is actually reaching the equipment that needs it.
